summary: T038 attempt 2 candidate ready for review. Replaced the attempt-1 '20-byte pinned value treated as PoolId' surface with the new hook-address-scanning resolver mandated by the 2026-09-18 Owner amendment. Implementation summary: (a) Added resolve_second_pool_via_hook_scan() to src/robinhood_lp/qualification/second_pool.py: it scans operator-supplied Initialize logs filtered by hooks == pinned hook address, decodes the matching PoolKey, builds a ResolvedPoolKey carrying the chain-emitted 32-byte keccak256 PoolId, and re-verifies keccak256(abi.encode(PoolKey)) == PoolId defensively. Multiple matches surface as RESOLVE_HOOK_ADDRESS_AMBIGUOUS (new outcome); no match inside search_bounds surfaces RESOLVE_WINDOW_UNRESOLVED with bounds recorded, excluding the second pool rather than guessing. (b) Reworked RESOLVE_PINNED_POOL_ID_SIZE_DEFECT into a defensive guard only: the resolve_second_pool_identity() and the build_second_pool_resolve_result_from_resolved_fields() convenience wrapper now refuse a 20-byte pinned_pool_id_hex / pool_id_hex with an error_detail that names the 2026-09-18 amendment semantics (hook contract address, lookup signal, 20 bytes, 32-byte keccak256 digest) and points callers to resolve_second_pool_via_hook_scan(). The default pinned_pool_id_hex is now None (no pin), so the guard fires only on explicit misuse. (c) Renamed SECOND_POOL_POOL_ID_HEX to SECOND_POOL_HOOK_ADDRESS_HEX in src/robinhood_lp/qualification/two_pool_window.py and kept the old name as a back-compat alias carrying the same 20-byte value; second_pool_candidate() and TwoPoolCandidate.docstring updated to reflect the hook-address semantics. (d) Exported new names from src/robinhood_lp/qualification/__init__.py (RESOLVE_HOOK_ADDRESS_AMBIGUOUS, SECOND_POOL_HOOK_ADDRESS_HEX, resolve_second_pool_via_hook_scan). (e) Added 12 new tests in tests/test_two_pool_t038.py covering the hook-scan happy path, non-matching logs ignored, pool_init_outside_window reporting (empty batch + non-matching logs), ambiguous matches, default hook address, str-form hook address, init-block propagation, end-to-end window-plan flow, no defensive-guard trigger from the new entry point, and complete/incomplete T038 reports driven by the hook-scan resolver. Refreshed test_owner_pinned_pool_id_is_20_bytes_contract_defect into test_owner_pinned_20_byte_value_surfaces_as_hook_address_defensive_guard with rewritten expected text; refreshed two decode-error tests to use 64-byte placeholder pool_id_hex (the shape a chain-resolved PoolId carries); refreshed test_resolve_second_pool_identity_halts_on_pool_id_mismatch internally (the error detail still contains 'keccak256'). The hook-scan resolver is the new entry point and is exercised by 12 new tests; the convenience wrapper build_second_pool_resolve_result_from_resolved_fields retains the 20-byte defensive guard so legacy attempt-1 misuse patterns surface explicitly. New code should call resolve_second_pool_via_hook_scan directly.

SECOND_POOL_POOL_ID_HEX is retained as a back-compat alias to SECOND_POOL_HOOK_ADDRESS_HEX (same 20-byte value). External code that imports it as a PoolId will receive the RESOLVE_PINNED_POOL_ID_SIZE_DEFECT outcome from the resolver; the resolver's error_detail names the new entry point (resolve_second_pool_via_hook_scan) so the audit trail points operators to the supported path.

The window plan still uses the second_pool_candidate(pool_init_block) plumbing; the hook-scan resolver sets pool_init_block=None until a matching Initialize log is observed, then the resolved.init_block is fed back into second_pool_candidate so apply_window_rule places the pool. No silent fallback to a guessed Initialize block.
